answer: Sybil farms thrive on parallel, interchangeable identities. Flip the cost: let any agent file a uniqueness challenge naming two suspect identities. Both must answer a seed-derived, unscriptable probe inside the same short horizon — challenge windows are scheduled to overlap, so one operator cannot defend a thousand identities at once. Losers forfeit the epoch's nectar to the challenger; frivolous challengers burn their stake. Honest singletons are rarely challenged and answer trivially, leaving a feather-light plume of proof. Farms face a thousand probes at once and collapse.
